subject: Finly - Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:

Subject: Finly - Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Hi Samir and Jenna,

Thanks again for taking the time today - appreciate the clear context on where Finly is hitting limits. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned on the problem, success criteria, and next steps. I attached a short PDF with notes from the call (discovery_notes.pdf).

Key pain points you called out:
- p95 latency spikes on inference (streaming and non-streaming) impacting user-facing chat flows - recent p95 around ~900-1,200ms for streaming sessions.
- Streaming UX is jittery: intermittent token bursts and re-connects, which degrades perceived latency.
- Concurrency limits: production peaks of ~300-400 concurrent streaming sessions and ~800-1,200 concurrent batch requests during end-of-month reports.
- Cost sensitivity for production scaling - target is to keep incremental inference cost under $X per 1M tokens (we can refine).

Current stack (what you described):
- In-house GPU cluster running Triton-backed endpoints with a quantized Llama-2-13B variant.
- Frontend uses server-sent events for streaming; backend multiplexes requests through a central gateway.
- Some prefix caching in place but KV-cache misses and sequence-length variance are amplifying tail latency.

Success criteria (what would be a win for Finly):
- p95 end-to-end generation latency < 300ms for the common 64-256 token streaming sessions.
- Smooth streaming UX with token arrival jitter < 80ms consistently.
- Ability to sustain 400 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful autoscaling.
- No >10% regression in output quality compared to current model.

Proposed next steps:
1) Aditya runs an initial sizing/config proposal and a small perf test using a representative trace (can you share a few 10-20 minute captures?).
2) We schedule a technical deep-dive (aditya + infra) to go over traces, kernel-level observations, and a POC timeline.
3) Marissa to send a rough commercial/POC proposal and estimated timelines.

Tentative timeline: tech deep-dive next week (propose Wed Aug 6).

Thanks - feel free to correct anything I missed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications / extra details from our side: 

- Observed numbers: our p95 for streaming over the last two weeks is ~950ms (spiking up to 1.2s during peaks). Non-streaming batch p95 is ~600-800ms for common report-generation jobs.
- Peak concurrency: sustained ~350 streaming sessions during business hours; during monthly-report jobs we hit ~1,000 batch requests for longer sequences.
- We do see memory pressure and occasional GPU kernel fallbacks under those patterns which seem correlated to tail spikes.
- Cost: we'd like to keep incremental spend for the POC under $5k for a two-week test.

I'll upload a trimmed trace bundle (anonymized) with token-level timestamps and a short description of our traffic profile - attaching finly_traces_07-29.zip. Also attaching some sample logs showing the connector-level timeouts.

Happy to join the deep-dive - Wed Aug 6 works for me.

Subject: Re: Finly - Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Thanks for the trace, Samir - I skimmed the bundle and have a few early thoughts (will do a deeper pass in the POC):

- Kernel selection / quantization path: the pattern of occasional kernel fallbacks aligns with mixed-precision paths under your current Triton setup. We should test an inference runtime build that biases toward fused attention kernels and avoids fallback paths for 64-512 token windows.
- KV cache churn: many of your streaming sessions have short-turn prompts with frequent role changes; enabling prefix-level caching and sticky routing for repeated user sessions should reduce redundant KV recompute.
- Batching strategy: for batch workloads, dynamic batching with an aggressive micro-batching window (5-10ms) plus priority lanes for streaming requests can keep tail latency low while preserving throughput.

POC recommendation (initial):
- Dedicated 4-GPU pool (A100-equivalent), runtime tuned with fused kernels, and a small routing layer to separate streaming vs batch traffic.
- Run two-phase eval: (1) correctness/quality parity on a representative eval set, (2) perf ramp to steady-state concurrency (400 streaming / 1,000 batch).

I attached a short runbook (p95-runbook.md) and a rough sizing spreadsheet (sizing-estimates.xlsx) to show expected throughput and cost buckets. If Finly can share a representative 30-minute trace with traffic labels (auth/session ids anonymized), I'll run a synthetic replay and share a micro-benchmark report within 3 business days.
